verdict.summary: Retailing has moved beyond bootstrap status into a credible RC-oriented Symfony 8.1 component with explicit ecosystem dependencies, database migrations, executable PHP quality gates, UI testing infrastructure, and recent canonical-topology hardening; remaining concerns are an unclean working tree, lack of an exact release tag, limited evidenced production-operability controls, and incomplete repository-level documentation evidence.
strengths: Symfony 8.1 and PHP 8.4 baseline is explicit and current.
Recent commits show focused RC hardening, canonical topology work, Cruding contract alignment, and executable quality-gate work.
Repository includes PHPStan, PHPUnit, PHP-CS-Fixer, schema parity checks, centralized Gating integration, and Playwright UI tests.
Component dependencies are explicitly integrated with Smartresponsor ecosystem packages through dev-master path repositories.
Persistence evolution is represented by multiple Doctrine migrations and schema validation scripts.
risks: Git working tree is not clean because CMCP_CHANGELOG.md is modified.
Current commit has no exact Git tag, reducing evidence of formal release packaging.
No concrete observability, alerting, deployment, rollback, or production runtime controls are evidenced by the supplied facts.
Repository-specific Antora navigation and index documentation are not evidenced.
Product-market validation is only weakly evidenced by repository metadata and cannot be strongly scored from code facts alone.
next_actions: Restore a clean working tree before declaring the current commit an RC baseline.
Run and archive the full composer gate, PHPStan, PHPUnit, schema parity, and Playwright results against the exact RC commit.
Create a formal release tag only after all acceptance gates pass.
Add or expose concise component documentation covering responsibility boundary, integration contracts, runtime expectations, and release procedure.
Document production-operability expectations such as logging, monitoring, deployment, rollback, and failure handling where those responsibilities belong to Retailing.
notes: Assessment is based only on the deterministic repository facts embedded in the authoritative prompt.
No repository mutations, staging, commits, or pushes were performed.
Runtime and operations scores are intentionally conservative because infrastructure presence is not equivalent to evidenced production behavior.

product.summary: Retailing has a clear repository identity as a retail marketplace Symfony bundle with explicit framework and ecosystem dependencies, but repository-level product documentation evidence remains limited.
risks: Component purpose is visible in composer metadata, but broader responsibility and user-facing behavior are not fully evidenced.
Repository-specific Antora index and navigation files are absent from the supplied facts.
improvements: Document the component responsibility boundary and primary retail workflows.
Add concise canonical component documentation tied to acceptance and release expectations.

architecture.summary: Architecture is strong for the evidenced scope, with a conventional Symfony-oriented source topology, explicit package boundaries, recent canonical-topology hardening, and aligned Smartresponsor component dependencies.
risks: Heavy dev-master ecosystem coupling makes compatibility dependent on coordinated repository evolution.
The supplied facts do not demonstrate all runtime contracts between the numerous dependent components.
improvements: Keep cross-component contracts executable and covered by acceptance tests.
Continue enforcing canonical Symfony topology and dependency-boundary checks through Gating.

runtime.summary: Runtime foundations are credible through Symfony 8.1, Doctrine ORM, migrations, fixtures, templates, and executable console integration, but production performance and resilience behavior are not directly evidenced.
risks: No latency, throughput, caching, load, retry, timeout, or failure-mode measurements are present in the supplied facts.
Runtime readiness cannot be inferred solely from framework and migration structure.
improvements: Capture representative runtime acceptance evidence for core retail workflows.
Add explicit resilience or performance checks where Retailing owns those concerns.

qa.summary: QA maturity is strong, with PHPStan, PHPUnit, PHP-CS-Fixer, schema parity scripts, centralized Gating, coverage support, and Playwright-based UI testing all evidenced in the repository.
risks: The supplied facts prove tool presence but do not include current pass/fail outputs for every gate.
A modified working tree weakens reproducibility of any unstated acceptance result.
improvements: Run the entire gate stack against the exact commit and retain deterministic pass evidence.
Keep unit, schema, static-analysis, style, and browser acceptance checks mandatory for RC promotion.

ops.summary: Delivery readiness is materially supported by GitHub workflows and centralized Gating, but production observability, deployment strategy, rollback, and operational monitoring are not evidenced by the supplied repository facts.
risks: No exact Git tag exists for the assessed commit.
Working tree contains a modified CMCP_CHANGELOG.md.
No concrete logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, deployment, or rollback configuration is evidenced.
improvements: Require a clean tree and complete gate evidence before release tagging.
Document or integrate the operational controls that apply to Retailing deployments.
Establish an immutable tagged RC baseline after acceptance.

market.summary: The component is clearly positioned as a retail marketplace capability and is integrated with catalog, collection, CRUD, table, location, object, interface, and viewing components, but external market validation is not available in the supplied repository evidence.
risks: No customer, adoption, revenue, conversion, or production-usage evidence is included.
Market fit cannot be reliably inferred from architecture alone.
improvements: Link product-level usage or acceptance evidence into the Atlas workflow when available.
Keep market scoring distinct from engineering maturity unless real product evidence is supplied.

overall.summary: Retailing is a solid RC candidate from an engineering perspective, especially in architecture and QA, but should not be treated as fully release-complete until the working tree is clean, all gates are evidenced on the exact commit, release tagging is formalized, and operational expectations are clearer.
risks: Current state is not a pristine reproducible release baseline.
Operational maturity is less evidenced than code and QA maturity.
Product-market evidence is insufficient for a strong market-readiness conclusion.
improvements: Produce a clean, fully gated, immutable RC commit.
Strengthen component documentation and production-operability evidence.
